title: Excessive Module Nesting (Single-File Modules)
pattern: Creating highly fragmented directory structures and individual module files that contain only a single, trivial function or struct.
why_bad: It results in 'directory explosion' and severe file-navigation friction. Developers spend more time switching files, navigating paths, and writing boilerplate `pub mod` declarations than reading or writing actual business logic.
detection: A module file containing fewer than 15 lines of active code (excluding imports and boilerplates), nested inside multiple layers of single-file subdirectories.
counterexample: Modules that isolate heavy, highly specialized algorithms (like custom crypto engines or parsing state machines) that must remain strictly isolated.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright, *Software Engineering at Google* (2020), Chapter 2 ("Software Engineering Over Time"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4.
